summary: Embedding endpoint returning mismatched metadata leading to rerank latency spikes across regions
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that calls to the embeddings endpoint intermittently return responses whose metadata (embedding_id and "namespace") do not match the payload order. Downstream reranker sees out-of-order candidate metadata and falls back to a CPU path, causing 2-6x tail latency spikes.

Impact:
- Affected customer: NimbleDocs (dedicated).
- Production traffic: rerank latency tail increases from ~120ms to 800-2,400ms during incidents.
- Result: UX timeouts in their search UI and elevated error rates reported by customer monitoring.

Environment:
- Redwood prod environment (vpc-dedicated) servicing NimbleDocs dedicated pool.
- Observed in us-east primary region; cascade effects seen in eu-west for cross-region traffic.

Observed behavior:
- Embeddings API returns batches where embedding payload order does not match embedding metadata array order in the JSON response (embedding_id / namespace misaligned).
- Reranker logs show candidate-to-metadata mismatches and triggers CPU fallback which increases tokenization and scoring latency.

Why this is critical:
- Dedicated customers rely on deterministic mapping between embeddings and metadata for correctness. Out-of-order metadata breaks top-k stability and increases latency and 5xxs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NimbleDocs account credentials and call POST /v1/embeddings with batch size 16 and client-supplied ids (embed_ids array) against prod us-east endpoint.
2) Immediately call POST /v1/rerank with the returned embeddings and matching ids in the same order.
3) Observe rerank score instability and tail latency >1s in ~1/200 requests.
4) Compare embedding_id order in embeddings response JSON to original request order; intermittently they differ.
5) Reproduce frequency increases when client uses parallelized client-side batching across multiple TCP connections.
6) Re-run traffic routed to eu-west after cross-region test to observe propagated latency.

comments: Maya Chen (Support) [2026-03-10]: Logged on behalf of NimbleDocs. Provided initial request/response body samples and a HAR capture. Customer seeing intermittent top-k noise and large latency spikes.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) [2026-03-10]: Assigned for triage. Initial hypothesis: parallel connection reuse + protobuf/gRPC muxing bug in embeddings-service response packing. Requesting pcap and exact client SDK version from customer.
NimbleDocs Support (customer) [2026-03-11]: Sent client SDK v0.9.3 and load pattern (16 concurrent workers, batches of 16). Observed peak on weekdays 09:00-11:00 ET.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) [2026-03-11]: Replayed traffic in staging using same SDK and concurrency. Unable to reproduce with single-region internal staging (no reorder). Enabled verbose logging in embeddings-service to capture response assembly ordering.

Priya Singh (Backend Eng) [2026-03-12]: Found a reassembly code path in embeddings-service that uses an async aggregator; under high concurrency a map iteration was non-deterministic. Patch PR prepared to enforce deterministic ordering by capturing original request index.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) [2026-03-12]: Deployed hotfix to canary in us-east. Observed reduction in reorder metric from 0.78% -> 0.02% in 2-hour window. Requesting extended verification from NimbleDocs on their traffic spike window.

NimbleDocs Support (customer) [2026-03-13]: Confirmed dramatic reduction in wrong-metadata events and tail latency; still seeing rare spikes (~1/20k). Customer requests RCA and long-term fix timeline.

Priya Singh (Backend Eng) [2026-03-13]: PR #8421 contains deterministic index tracking; additional integration tests added for parallel clients. Scheduling full rollout to dedicated pools after QA signoff.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) [2026-03-13]: Marking as in-progress. Need to verify eu-west replica behavior and update canary config to include a cross-region test. Linking to INT-1203 for router investigation.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: non-deterministic iteration over map/aggregation buffer in embeddings-service async aggregator produced response arrays with permuted order under concurrent writes.
Evidence: Staging replay with same SDK and concurrency produced identical symptom only after enabling interleaved response assembly; disabling connection pooling removed symptom.
Root cause seems to be a race in response assembly when multiple write goroutines append to a shared slice without preserving client-provided indices.

Related observation: envoy/upstream connection reuse and HTTP/2 stream multiplexing increased the window for concurrent assembly; router metrics show slight increase in stream resets for some backends.
Change introduced in commit ab12f3 (async aggregator refactor) likely introduced the bug; PR referenced below reintroduces stable ordering by tracking original request positions.

Residual rare spikes may be caused by cross-region replication lag when eu-west reranker pulls cached metadata and experiences transient inconsistency; further investigation with regional cache invalidation required.
resolution: Hotfix deployed to canary in us-east (2026-03-12): embeddings-service updated to preserve client-specified index positions during async aggregation. Canary metrics: reorder rate fell from 0.78% to 0.02%. Pending full rollout to all dedicated pools and cross-region verification. Follow-up work: INT-1203 to examine router connection pooling settings and an integration test added to CI for multi-connection client replay. Customer notified and will receive final RCA and change window for scheduled rollout.
